title: Integrality of Averages of Roots of Unity and Perfect Isometries
summary: We establish a criterion for the integrality of averages of roots of unity and apply it to settle a conjecture regarding the linearity of functions on $\mathbb{Z}_n$. Specifically, we prove that for any modulus $n \ge 1$, if a function $f: \mathbb{Z}_n \to \mathbb{Z}_n$ satisfies that the averages $\frac{1}{n} \sum_{x=0}^{n-1} ω^{f(x)+bx}$ (where $ω=e^{2πi/n}$) are algebraic integers for all $b \in \mathbb{Z}_n$, then $f$ is necessarily linear modulo $n$.
